crossRefs.note: No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone as a pledge, for he takes a life in pledge.
When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not go into his house to get his pledge.
You shall not deprive the foreigner or the fatherless of justice, nor take a widow’s clothing in pledge;
For you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor,
Take the garment of one who puts up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in pledge for a wayward woman.
If you don’t have means to pay, why should he take away your bed from under you?
and has not wronged any, but has restored to the debtor his pledge, has taken nothing by robbery, has given his bread…
hasn’t wronged any, hasn’t taken anything to pledge, hasn’t taken by robbery, but has given his bread to the hungry…
if the wicked restore the pledge, give again that which he had taken by robbery, walk in the statutes of life…
and they lay themselves down beside every altar on clothes taken in pledge; and in the house of their God they drink…

translations.web: If you take your neighbor’s garment as collateral, you shall restore it to him before the sun goes down,
translations.bsb: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
translations.kjv: If thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, thou shalt deliver it unto him by that the sun goeth down:
translations.asv: If thou at all take thy neighbor's garment to pledge, thou shalt restore it unto him before the sun goeth down:
